---
title: "AI functions on tables"
description: "Call an AI function on a column: in mutate() and filter(), each distinct value sent once, in parallel."
---

{{< include ../_setup.qmd >}}

Much of the work AI functions do is on tables: tag every ticket, extract
fields from every invoice, flag every complaint. Called on a
[dpyr](https://github.com/MaximeRivest/dpyr) column instead of a value,
an AI function becomes a **column expression**, usable in `mutate()` and
`filter()` like any other.

```{python}
from typing import Literal
from dpyr import read, col, n

@ai
def intent(user_query: str) -> Literal["booking", "cancelation", "information", "complaint"]:
    """The hotel guest's intent."""

@ai
def reply(user_query: str, tone: str) -> str:
    """A one-sentence reply to the guest, in the given tone."""

inbox = read([                        # or read("inbox.parquet"), a dataframe, ...
    {"id": 1, "user_query": "Book me a room for two nights."},
    {"id": 2, "user_query": "The room was dirty and nobody answered the phone!"},
    {"id": 3, "user_query": "Cancel my stay, the noise was unbearable."},
    {"id": 4, "user_query": "Is there parking?"},
    {"id": 5, "user_query": "Book me a room for two nights."},
])

inbox.mutate(intent=intent(col.user_query))
```

Columns and constants mix freely: here the tone is the same for every row.

```{python}
inbox.mutate(answer=reply(col.user_query, tone="formal")).select(col.id, col.answer)
```

And the result can be grouped, filtered and summarized like any column:

```{python}
@ai
def is_unhappy(user_query: str) -> bool:
    """Is the guest unhappy about something?"""

(inbox
    .filter(is_unhappy(col.user_query))
    .mutate(intent=intent(col.user_query))
    .group_by(col.intent)
    .summarize(n=n()))
```

## How it runs

- **Nothing runs when the line is written**, but the column's type (the
  return annotation) is checked straight away.
- **Each distinct input goes to the model once** (rows 1 and 5 above
  cost one call), 8 at a time, and the answers are remembered for the
  session.
- **Showing a table only asks for the rows it shows.**
- **A row that fails raises after every row has run**, and running again
  retries only the failures. `errors="null"` keeps going with nulls.
- **The prompt is fixed when the line is written**, so optimizing the
  function later never mixes old and new answers in one column.

Options go through `vectorize`:

```{python}
#| eval: false
inbox.mutate(intent=intent.vectorize(threads=16, errors="null")(col.user_query))
```

## The run itself: `fn.map`

`fn.map(table)` runs the function on every row and returns the whole run
table: the predictions, plus the error, time and tokens of each row. It
is `evaluate` without the scoring.

```{python}
intent.map(inbox.select(col.user_query)).select(col.user_query, col.pred_result, col.input_tokens)
```
